As a class, we need to familiarize ourselves with Disability terminology so that we avoid accidental offense in this class and beyond. Many of our readings in this first week discuss Disability Language (even while addressing the importance of experiential disability, geographical place, and time). Referencing the texts we've read, videos we've watched, and terminological resources provided in week one, let's set discuss what we've learned about acceptable and unacceptable terminology. (Acknowledging that we’re all human and mistakes will be and have been made but that each of us has good intentions, let's be kind here!)

 

Directions for Post and Conversation: 
--------------------------------------

* Write a response to what you've learned this week; you might share your own thoughts or analysis, pose a question to the group to clarify understanding, address nuances or exceptions that you've considered, discuss your own personal experience with disability language do's and don'ts, etc.

* The only requirements for this first discussion are thoughtfulness, obvious engagement with at least one assigned work from this week, at least one respectful interaction with another's post, and a minimum word count of 150 words.

 

Though this discussion post will remain open throughout the semester, the deadline

by which you must post and respond to this discussion is Friday, August 21st by 11:59PM.

You must post before then to receive graded credit without penalty.

events.title: Introduction: More than a Name Tag [RHAB 3000.401 (12813)]
events.notes:
----------------------
Welcome to the course!
----------------------

As future helping professionals, one of the most valuable skills you will develop is the ability to build meaningful relationships. Before we begin exploring ethics, professionalism, and the responsibilities of helping others, let's take some time to get to know one another. This course will be richer if we learn from each other's experiences, perspectives, and goals.

Even if you do not plan to enter the helping profession, the course content can benefit your future career!

One of my most frequently stated ideas related to learning from one another is “I already know everything I know. To learn and grow, it is important for me to learn what others know.”

Rather than simply sharing your name and major, use this discussion as an opportunity to introduce the person behind the student.

------------
Initial Post
------------

Write an introduction consisting of at least two well-developed paragraphs. Academic writing defines a paragraph as

* typically ranging from 100 – 200 words

* including a minimum of 5 and up to 8 sentences

* with a topic sentence, supporting details, and a concluding sentence

This length allows for depth, evidence, and analysis while keeping it focused on one idea.

Your writing should reflect the quality expected of a university senior and demonstrate thoughtful reflection. While there is no single correct way to introduce yourself, consider addressing many of the following:

* What led you to pursue a career in addiction counseling or another helping profession?

* Is there a particular population or setting where you hope to work after graduation? Why?

* What professional accomplishment would you like to achieve within the next ten years?

* Describe a life experience, mentor, volunteer opportunity, or job that has influenced your career goals.

* What personal qualities or strength do you believe will make you an effective helping professional?

* What is one skill you hope to strengthen during this course?

* Outside of school and work, what activities, hobbies, or interests help you maintain balance and wellness?

* Share one interesting fact about yourself that your classmates would not likely know from reading your résumé.

Finally, conclude your post by answering the following question:

* If your future clients could describe you using only three words after working with you, what would you hope those three words would be and why?

There is no right or wrong answer. This is simply an opportunity to begin reflecting on the kind of professional you hope to become.

-----------------------
Response to a Classmate
-----------------------

After posting your introduction, respond to at least one classmate.

At least one well-developed paragraph is required. Move beyond statements such as "I agree," "Nice to meet you," or "Good post."

Your response should:

* Identify something you found interesting or meaningful in your classmate's introduction.

* Ask at least one thoughtful follow-up question that encourages continued conversation.

* Make a meaningful connection between your classmate's experiences and your own or discuss how their perspective broadens your thinking.

Remember that professional communication includes demonstrating respect, curiosity, and encouragement. Your goal is to begin building a supportive learning community that will benefit everyone throughout the semester.

----------------------------
Writing Quality & Formatting
----------------------------

As this is a junior-level university course, your discussion posts should demonstrate professional communication and thoughtful reflection.

* Before submitting your work, proofread for grammar, spelling, punctuation, and clarity.

* Write in complete sentences and organized paragraphs.

* Support your ideas with thoughtful explanation rather than brief responses.

* Maintain a respectful and professional tone.

* Contribute meaningfully to the discussion rather than simply answering the prompts.

Should you find the need for assistance with writing, reach out to the [UNT Writing Center.] (https://writingcenter.unt.edu/)

I look forward to learning more about each of you and following your journey as you prepare to enter the addiction counseling profession.

Grading

This discussion is graded in 3 specific areas: 

* Your Initial Post

* Your Response to classmate

* Writing Quality and Formatting

events.title: Who Are You? Assignment (Due Week 3) [HNRS 1000.002 (6788)]
events.notes:
“Who Are You” Assignment  

Assignment description: 

This assignment asks you to think about who you are and how you hope to develop and grow as an Honors College student at UNT. You are invited to introspect about the experiences, relationships, and aspects of your life journey that have shaped your passions, academic interests, and career goals. You should be intentional about exploring “who you are,” as it will inform how you approach your Honors College education and membership in our Honors College community. You are also asked to look ahead – what do you hope to accomplish while at UNT and in your life and career after graduation. This assignment also gives you the opportunity to share more about yourself with your peers, fostering new connections within our class.  

This assignment is comprised of three related components. 1) Creating an artifact/project that visually represents who you are; 2) writing a short reflection paper that explores the intentional choices you made while creating your artifact/project; 3) participating in a class presentation/discussion in which you share your creative artifact/project with your classmates.  

Be intentional, but don’t overthink things. Have fun with the assignment! Embrace the chance to creatively share about yourself with your classmates! 

Overall points available: 60 points total 

* Creative artifact/project: 25 points 

* Presentation: 20 points

* Reflection/Process paper: 15 points 

 

Creative artifact/project: 

The largest portion of this assignment is to create a visual representation of yourself in response to the question, “Who are you?” It is entirely up to you what format this takes. Choose the format that best matches your style, strengths, interests, and abilities. This creative project should look backward at your past and forward into your future. It will likely include aspects of you and your family’s personal journeys and reflection on your community(ies) of origin. It should reflect your present, as an Honors College student at UNT. And, it should look toward your future, calling upon your passions, interests, goals, and hopes/dreams. You chose what is most important to tell the story of “who you are” and who you hope to be. 

Here are some potential options, but don’t feel limited to these ideas – push the creative limits (or not) in a way that is best suited to you. 

* Poster with visual model representing aspects of “you” 

* Twitter X feed telling your story (fake/non-published is fine) 

* Blog post biography/wiki article (fake/non-published is fine) 

* Physical model/diorama  

* Hand drawn pictographs 

Remember, you only have one week to work on this assignment, so it does not have to be the most polished final product. But it should demonstrate intentionality, thoughtfulness, and adequate time to compile. The spirit of the assignment should be evident in your work – that's the most important part! 

To receive full credit you must: 

* Submit a copy/photo of your creative project by the assigned due date.  

* Fully respond to the prompt in your creative project.  

* Demonstrate intentional choices and thorough engagement with the assignment 

 

Relevant course objective:

Students will be able to articulate academic identity, cultivate passion, and establish goals within an Honors College framework.  

Assignment objectives: 

* To facilitate introductions between classmates and strengthen our sense of community within the class. 

* To think intentionally about who students are as they enter their Honors College education and how they intend to benefit from membership in the Honors College. 

* To creatively express ideas that demonstrate critical thinking and abstract conceptualization.

Connect with your Peer Instructor [HNRS 1000.002 (6788)]
events.notes:
Networking with staff, faculty, and your peers is a primary goal of the Honors College, as it contributes greatly to your personal and professional development. Thus, this assignment will allow you to either start or continue networking with someone whom you can very much benefit building a deeper connection with: our HNRS 1000 peer instructors! These students are experienced UNT and Honors College students who can serve as mentors and provide insight on how to navigate academics in the Honors College and campus life at UNT.

Reflect on the questions below, and reach out to your Peer Instructor(s) with your answers. You should email both peer instructors (emails listed on the syllabus). They will provide individual responses to your emails after that date, at which point you can decide whether or not to continue the conversation.

Please title your email "HNRS 1000 Peer Instructor Assignment" in the subject line. 

Academic Focus

* What’s your major, and why did you choose it?

* What do you hope to do after college?

* Is there anything specific you’d like to do in this class?

Personal Interests

* Tell me a little about yourself!

* Are there things in life you really HATE?!!

* Are there things in life you really LOVE?!!

* Is there anything you’re really proud of?

* Are there any favorite events that you like to attend?

College Life

* Do you do anything outside of school you’d like to share? (Clubs? Sports? Cadets? Hobbies? etc.)

* What’s your go-to campus dining spot or meal?

* What are your favorite spots on campus?

* What is the most valuable of all campus resources you've used here at UNT?

* How have you handled being away from home/being homesick?

events.title: Who Are You? Process Reflection Paper (Due Week 4) [HNRS 1000.002 (6788)]
events.notes:
“Who Are You” Assignment  

Reflection paper
The final portion of this assignment is a brief reflection paper in which you will explain the intentional choices you made while constructing your creative project. This is your opportunity to explain what you have made and why you made it. This paper can be less formal/rigid in word choice, style, and tone; however, remember that it should still be appropriate for a class submission and reflect high-quality spelling and grammar. You may write about whatever is most relevant to you; however, consider responding to some of these questions in your paper: 

* Why did you choose your particular mode of creative expression for this assignment? 

* Which aspects of your life journey, passions, experiences, goals, etc. were most important for you to center in your project? 

* What intentional choices did you make while designing your creative artifact/project? Why? 

* How did a creative form of expression help/enable you to more fully tell your story (as opposed to a traditional essay)? 

* Was this assignment easier or harder for you than a traditional essay? Why? 

* What did you learn about yourself throughout this process? 

 

To receive full credit, you must: 

* Submit a 300 – 400 word reflection paper that demonstrates professional formatting and accurate spelling/grammar.  

* Clearly and fully respond to the prompt.  

* Demonstrate thoughtful reflection on your creative artifact/project.

Grading Rubric:

Required Item

Description

Points

PowerPoint 

Must be turned in on PowerPoint.

15 points

* Appearance, including:

You may use the Problems Faced by College Students List provided in the module content or select one of your own. 

May include more than one but must also include resources to address any other issues. 

10 points

Resource 1 - located on UNT campus

Resource 2 - located in or near the town you live

* Resource Name

100 points

(10 points/required item)

Images & Alt Text

* 1 image as client photo.

* 2nd image can be located anywhere in the presentation.

* Images must relate to the slide in which it is placed

* Do not simply place two images on the final slide. Use them within the presentation slides.

Authenticity

events.title: Me & UNT - Outside of Class Assignment [HNRS 1000.002 (6788)]
events.notes:
Exploring Our Homespace Assignment

This is a "walkabout" assignment that encourages you to engage with our campus as a "text." We can embrace our campus (or any place) as a living textbook that helps us gain first-hand experience exploring a location's heritage, culture, and social dynamics. By walking around with the intent to observe deeply and engage mindfully, we can learn a tremendous amount about the places we inhabit and the people we move alongside. UNT is our "homespace" - let's explore it together!

What's Due? (Let's start with the deliverable.)

It may be helpful to know what you are responsible for producing before discussing the assignment's details. After concluding the "walkabout," each group will upload a joint post on our "Me & UNT" discussion board. The post should include a PDF file (either of PowerPoint slides, Google Slides, or a compiled Word Document) and list the names of all group members. Each student is then expected to review their classmates' posts and comment on at least two. Your comments should be meaningful, as explained in the discussion post rubric. 

Your Task

Your group should pick a starting place for your "walkabout." Then, you should spend between 45 and 50 minutes walking around campus to complete this assignment. As a team, you are to look for patterns (mapping), notice all kinds of details (from signage to sidewalk design) (observing), and discover how people use our campus spaces (listening). You should track your walk (in any format, such as hand-drawn or digital). [Include a "map" of your walk in your submission.]

* First, visit at least two academic buildings. One that you have all been in previously, and one that none of you have visited. Consider questions such as these as you visit each space:

* What is the nature of the building, and how does it fit into the campus as a whole?

* Who uses the building? What makes you think so?

* How is the building organized both inside and outside?

* Talk to people who are using the space. What are they doing there?

* Take pictures - [Submission should include photos of these spaces, and a bullet-point list of reflections based on these questions - nothing formal.]

* Second, complete a color walk as you travel from your first building to the second. If the buildings are too close together, do the color walk after you visit both buildings. As a group, select a color. I'd stay away from green or black. :) Your goal is to be "super noticers." Try to notice every single occurrence of your color as you travel between spaces. 

* Take pictures - [Submission should include photos of some examples of your color on campus.]

* Third, decide on two of your group's favorite places on campus. It's up to you to choose your locations. Visit them - be sure you're still mapping!

* Your task is to visit each space, and then observe the space using all five senses (smell, touch, sight, hearing, taste(?)) - [Submission should include photos of each space and your descriptors.]

 

Relevant Course Objectives:

4. Engage in practices that cultivate care, belonging, and wellness as an active member of the HC community. 

Assignment Objectives:

1. To connect with other members of the Honors College community and strengthen our sense of community within the class

2. Learning to navigate campus and various spaces within the Denton community.

Research Proposal Project Intro

Research and Thesis experiences are a unique and valuable aspect of a student's Honors College experience. While a full research project or thesis are much more extensive and can span multiple semesters, this abbreviated project is designed to help you become familiar with the process of thinking about research, connecting with faculty, and determining whether or not this is something you'd like to pursue in the future. In-Class Discussion & Breakout

During the last class day, students will engage in small group discussions on how this semester has impacted and changed their goals that they wrote about in their papers.
